newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares start mixed, outlook weaker.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares start mixed, outlook weaker.

text.p: Singapore shares opened mixed on Monday with buyers sidelined ahead of this week's meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve and the approach of Friday's Lunar New Year holiday, dealers said.
"The immediate effect will be a downward bias on our market," one dealer said of his expectations for the week ahead.
A cautious opening 90 minutes of trade in Singapore saw the OUB over the counter index slip 4.05 to 1,275.67 while the key Straits Times Industrials Index edged up 4.84 to 2,221.31.
Early volume was mild with 68.8 million units traded producing 130 losers to 89 gainers.
Initial interest was in technology counters with troubled IPC Corp leading volume after trade in its stock resumed on Monday following its suspension last week.
At 0230 GMT, 12.3 million IPC shares had changed hands, producing a fall of Singapore $0.09 at S$0.47.
Creative Technology, which revealed much improved second half profits on Saturday, led gainers up S$2.30 at S$20.60 on slim volume of 227,550 shares.
